Subject: Request: Data flow mapping + SIG evidence for procurement review

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well — we’re progressing Redwood through our procurement review and the security team has a couple of final asks before we complete the vendor risk assessment. Specifically: 

- A data flow diagram showing where customer data enters Redwood, any third-party subprocessors that handle or persist data, and high-level controls in place for each hop.
- Answers to a handful of SIG questions around cryptographic key management (KMS/HSM), encryption at rest and in transit, and tokenization/sensitive-field handling.
- Copies or redacted excerpts of your latest SOC 2 report and any evidence bundles you normally share with customers (subprocessor attestation, contracts, config screenshots).

Can you let us know what you can provide and an expected timeline? Ideally we’d have these artifacts for legal by end of next week (Oct 29). If there’s a preferred contact for technical details I can loop them in.

Thanks — Oliver
Oliver Grant
Manager, Information Security

Oliver — thanks for the follow-ups. Sharing the answers below so you can paste them into the SIG form; attached is the evidence bundle and our redacted SOC 2. If you need additional screenshots or a live walkthrough, Karthik can join a quick call.

Quick KMS & crypto summary (for SIG SC-7):
- Key custody: Redwood supports both customer-managed keys (CMK) via customer KMS integrations (customer-supplied AWS KMS / GCP KMS keys) and Redwood-managed keys. For customers who bind a CMK, all data-at-rest encryption and SQL-level column encryption use keys wrapped by the customer KMS.
- Redwood-managed KMS: keys are stored in our managed HSM-backed service (FIPS 140-2 L3) and are wrapped under a root HSM key. Decryption operations are audited and require RBAC approval with MFA for key rotation. Only a small set of security engineers (Karthik and two others) have emergency access via an audited break-glass process.
- Encryption in transit: All network communications between customer clients and Redwood endpoints use TLS1.3. Inter-service traffic inside our VPC uses mTLS with mutual certs.
- Tokens & embeddings: Persistent tokens and derived embeddings are encrypted at rest. Retention windows are configurable per customer; default retention for derivations is 90 days. For customers who provision CMKs, per-customer encryption uses their keys; otherwise platform keys are used.
- Logging & audit: Key use events are logged to an append-only audit store and exported to our SIEM; SOC 2 controls validate logging retention and review cadence.

Attachments included in Drive bundle and zipped evidence: 
- SOC2_report_redacted.pdf (redacted control narratives and report pages)
- sig-evidence-bundle.zip (screenshots: KMS console showing key policies, key rotation jobs, sample access logs; contract excerpts with subprocessors)
- kms_architecture_note.pdf (short technical note authored by Karthik on key wrapping and emergency access)
- redwood_subprocessor_list_v1.csv (authoritative list of subprocessors, data categories processed, and retention windows)
- data_flow_diagram_v2.png (high-level flow called out in the diagram)

If you want a version of the data-flow that separates PII vs non-PII paths, tell us and we’ll produce that by Oct 26. Otherwise, we’ll mark the request completed in HubSpot HS-982173 and share the Drive link (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cDF-example).

Karthik — would you add one-line confirmation about the emergency access process here?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
